findings.title: Both Anthropic Skills list walks paginate on a cursor the API never returns
findings.measured: the live list envelope is {data, has_more, next_page}; there is no last_id, and the forward cursor is the `page` query parameter. Both walks advance on has_more + last_id -> after_id, so both terminate after page 1.
findings.blastRadius: both walks request limit=100, so a <=100-version history and a <=100-skill workspace behave correctly today (assuming the server honors the requested page size, which it did at limit=1 in C4). Past 100 versions the GC deletes only the first page and the subsequent skill delete is REFUSED (live check C5 confirmed the server enforces versions-before-skill). It does NOT wedge the whole reclaim: AnthropicSkillGcEngine isolates per-skill failures — the throw is caught into `errors`, local sync rows are deliberately retained so a later run resumes, and the run returns ok:false. The real consequence is a NON-CONVERGING reclaim: every later GC run re-deletes the same first 100 versions (idempotent 404s), fails the skill delete again, and surfaces the same error forever; the remote skill is never reclaimed. That is still precisely the failure S0's 'paginate to exhaustion before any deleteSkill' deliverable set out to remove. Past 100 custom skills, a display_title collision rethrows instead of adopting the existing remote identity, so a lost create response can strand a skill.
findings.evidence: live-results.json checks C3 + C4; deterministic replay in packages/llm/src/__tests__/anthropic-skills-api-wire-conformance.test.ts (2 expected-fail tests)
findings.action: NOT patched in this lane — product defect, routed for filing per the lane brief

findings.title: The 30,000,000-byte upload gate is stricter than the live API
findings.measured: a canonical rooted zip of 30,000,505 archive bytes (30,000,169 uncompressed) was ACCEPTED by POST /v1/skills with HTTP 200.
findings.blastRadius: a confirmed client-side false rejection relative to observed server behavior — a conservative compatibility mismatch. Large-but-valid bundles are refused at sync and preflight. No data-loss or over-delete risk, and no DOCUMENTED supported limit has been contradicted, so severity stays LOW. S0 wrote that this constant 'changes only on that evidence' — this live boundary probe is that evidence.
findings.action: NOT changed in this lane — the constant is a product decision; routed for filing

findings.title: The 8-per-request container.skills ceiling is stated and enforced by the server
findings.measured: 8 distinct uploaded custom skills in one container.skills request were ACCEPTED; 9 were REJECTED with an explicit server-side validation message naming both the ceiling and the count: 'container.ContainerParams.skills: List should have at most 8 items after validation, not 9'.
findings.note: confirms the epic's core premise, and the quoted message is why this is more than an inference from a status code. Still a single observation on one workspace, not proof of a universal permanent cap. cinatra's hard cap of 8 matches the ceiling the API itself names.

findings.title: Unresolvable container.skills references fail closed at the API boundary
findings.measured: a syntactically valid but non-existent skill id was REJECTED by POST /v1/messages.
findings.note: a stale local sync mapping surfaces as an error rather than silently delivering nothing — the same fail-closed posture AnthropicSkillNotSyncedError enforces locally.

findings.title: display_title workspace-uniqueness is server-enforced and the shipped predicate matches the real body
findings.measured: a second create with the same display_title was rejected 4xx, and the shipped isDisplayTitleConflict predicate matches the real error body.
